title: A Probe Direction Is a Property of Its Prompt
hook: Two published studies disagree about whether bigger models better sense they're being evaluated. Both trends are reproducible from one design — by changing only the prompt.
key_points: Probes for 'the model knows it's being tested' contrast activations on evaluation-announcing prompts against ordinary ones, then report separation on held-out cases.
The method has an undisclosed free parameter: which prompt counts as 'announcing an evaluation' is a choice among many, and holding task text fixed while varying it moves the score.
Two published studies that disagree about the direction of the scaling trend are both reproducible from a single design by prompt choice alone.
The model under study accounts for only a small share of variance in the number reported about it; most lies in model-prompt interaction.
Consequence: collecting more evaluation items cannot repair the measurement, but varying prompts can.
A control finds the scored split is largely separable from surface form alone — a direction carrying no evaluation information still reproduces a substantial fraction of each published score.
content_html: If a model behaves differently when it senses it's being tested, our evaluations are compromised — so a line of work tries to read that sense straight off the activations. The recipe is standard: contrast activations on prompts that announce an evaluation against prompts that don't, extract a direction, report how well it separates held-out cases, and compare that number across models and against scale.
extra_html:
Noël's observation is that the instrument has a dial its readings don't report. "A prompt that announces an evaluation" isn't a prompt; it's a choice among many, and nothing in the method pins it down. Hold the task text fixed, vary only that choice, and the reported score moves — and so does the direction in which it trends with model size. Two published studies that disagree about the sign of that trend are both reproducible from a single design, by prompt choice alone.

Reframed as a measurement-design problem, the variance decomposition is damning: the model under study accounts for a small share of the variance in the number reported about it, and most of the rest is how each model responds to each prompt. That has a sharp practical corollary — adding evaluation items cannot repair the measurement, because item noise isn't the problem; varying prompts can. A further control lands harder still: the scored split is largely separable from surface form alone, so a direction carrying no evaluation information whatsoever still reproduces a substantial fraction of each published score. The paper concludes single-prompt designs can't support cross-model comparison, and gives a target number of prompts for one that can.

related.title: Internal-State Probes Read the Situation, Not the Action
related.hook: Probes that seem to detect an LLM's harmful intent before it acts mostly just detect the prompt's topic — three careful tests find they don't predict future misbehavior.

related.title: SAE Interventions Are Unreliable
related.hook: Clamping a 'harmful' sparse-autoencoder feature looks like it stops bad behavior — but this paper recovers it 95.8% of the time, exposing the gap between feature-level and real control.

related.title: What LLM Forecasters Know but Don't Say
related.hook: A forecasting model's chain-of-thought can look untouched by evidence that actually flipped its answer — but its hidden activations give the real story away.

flashcards.prompt: What hidden free parameter does this paper identify in evaluation-awareness probing?

choices.text: Which specific prompt is used to 'announce an evaluation' — a choice the method never fixes
Which layer of the network activations are read from
The regularization strength of the linear probe

flashcards.explanation_html: "A prompt that announces an evaluation" is not one prompt but a family of them. Holding task text fixed and varying only that choice moves the reported score and even the sign of its scaling trend.

flashcards.prompt: Why can't you fix this measurement by collecting more evaluation items?
flashcards.back_html: The variance lives in model-prompt interaction, not in item sampling noise. More items shrink the wrong error bar; varying prompts is what addresses the actual source.

flashcards.prompt: What does the surface-form control show?
flashcards.back_html: The scored split is largely separable from surface form alone, so a direction carrying no information about evaluation at all still reproduces a substantial fraction of each published score.

flashcards.prompt: What is the paper's conclusion about comparing models with these probes?

choices.text: A single-prompt design cannot support model-to-model comparison
The probes are valid, but only for models above a certain scale
Activation probing should be abandoned in favor of behavioral evaluation

flashcards.explanation_html: The paper treats the prompt as a facet of measurement design rather than an implementation detail, and gives the number of prompts a defensible comparison requires.
